cards.text: The prophet Ezekiel says the word of the LORD came to him. God tells him to mark out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon, both starting from the same land, with a signpost where they split. Friend, Ezekiel's a prophet AND the road crew now.

cards.question: Ezekiel marks one road for the sword of the king of Babylon to come against Judah, into fortified Jerusalem. Where does the other road go?

cards.text: Now the king of Babylon is standing at the fork, right where the two roads meet, and he's gotta pick one. Friend, I circle a parking lot three times just to pick a SPOT, and this man's picking a whole city.

cards.question: Standing at the fork with two roads in front of him, the king of Babylon makes up his mind by stopping to seek ___.

cards.text: He shakes the arrows, he consults the idols, he examines the liver. When I can't decide, I flip a coin, and this man is out here reading a LIVER.

cards.question: True or false: when the omen shows up in the right hand of the king of Babylon, it points him toward Rabbah of the Ammonites.
The omen says Jerusalem. What does the king of Babylon plan to direct against the gates of Jerusalem?

cards.text: Battering rams, a battle cry, a ramp, a siege wall. This man didn't pack for a visit, friend, he packed for a STAY.

cards.question: To the people who have sworn allegiance to the king of Babylon, the omen will seem false. But it will draw attention to their ___ and take them captive.

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD says the guilt is out in the open now, with sins "revealed in all your deeds". That's not one embarrassing reply-all, friend, that's reply-all on EVERYTHING.

cards.question: True or false: the Lord GOD says the ones whose sins have come to remembrance will be let go.

cards.text: Then God calls out one man, the "profane and wicked prince of Israel". Friend, nothing good ever comes after somebody says your full title like THAT.

cards.question: God tells the profane and wicked prince of Israel that the day has come for his ___ punishment.
With the prince of Israel facing his final punishment, the Lord GOD gives an order. What does He say to remove?
God says things will not remain as they are. He says to exalt the ___ and bring low the exalted.

cards.text: The lowly go up, the exalted come down. Then God says, "A ruin, a ruin, I will make it a ruin!" and friend, after three of those, I do NOT need to hear a fourth.

cards.question: God says the ruin will not be restored until something happens. What is it?

answers.text: The arrival of the One it belongs to
The end of seventy long years
The fall of the king of Babylon

cards.text: Now God tells Ezekiel to prophesy about the Ammonites and their contempt. Remember Rabbah, the city at the end of that other road?

cards.question: True or false: since the omen pointed to Jerusalem, God says the Ammonites are in the clear.

cards.text: A sword is drawn for them too, polished to flash like lightning. And while false visions and lying divinations are going around, that sword is headed for the necks of the wicked, whose day has come.

cards.question: God says, "Return the sword to its sheath!" Then where does He say the judging will happen?

answers.text: In the land of their origin

cards.text: God says He will pour out His anger and breathe the fire of His fury. Then He will hand them over to brutal men, skilled in destruction.

cards.question: The ruin God spoke of earlier had an 'until' attached to it. What is the very last thing God says about the ones in this final message?

findings.problem: The question asks which thing the king of Babylon directs against Jerusalem's gates. The wrong answers 'Wooden towers' and 'Fire pits' are not real details from the Bible. Siege works that do appear in Scripture, such as a siege ramp or siege towers (Isaiah 23:13), would be real details, but a ramp is in this passage, so pick details that appear nowhere in Ezekiel 21:18-32.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The statement says 'the ones whose sins have come to remembrance.' In Ezekiel 21:24 the people themselves come to remembrance ('because you have come to remembrance'). Their sins are 'revealed,' and the text never says the sins come to remembrance.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Ezekiel 21:27 ends with 'to whom I have assigned the right of judgment.' This is a key detail about the One the ruin waits for, and no card ever tells it. The card cites all of 21:27 but only covers the first half.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Ezekiel 21:30 begins 'Return the sword to its sheath!' and then says 'In the place where you were created... I will judge you.' The text leaves open who 'you' is: the sword (Babylon) or the Ammonites. The question and the answer 'In the land of their origin' assume the Ammonites.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'In the land of Babylon' could be argued right. If the 'you' told to return the sword to its sheath is Babylon, then the land of its origin is Babylon.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: 'Then He will hand them over' says 'them' to mean the Ammonites. Like 21:30, Ezekiel 21:31 speaks to an unnamed 'you.' The word 'Then' also adds an order of events that the text's list doesn't give.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup says 'The ruin God spoke of earlier had an 'until' attached to it.' That contrast tells the baker this message has no 'until,' which rules out the wrong answers 'They will be restored later' and 'They will rule once more.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'The ones in this final message' doesn't say who or what the message is about. The baker can't see the earlier cards, so the question needs to give its own context. That context still has to leave open who 'you' is, as noted for 21:30-31.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.
